newsitem.title: FRANCE: OECD says dollar/euro could be main currency pair.
newsitem.headline: OECD says dollar/euro could be main currency pair.

text.p: The dollar and European single currency, or euro, could become the most traded international currency pair, the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development(OECD) said on Thursday.

The OECD estimated the euro would have a 55 percent share of foreign exchange sales and purchases after intra-European currency trade disappears, lower than the dollar at 82 percent but larger than the yen at 24 percent.

"This share will still be large, and, given the size of the domestic EMU market, along with the historically low share of the use of the yen, the dollar and the euro could become the most frequently traded currency pair in the medium term," it said in its latest economic review.
The calculations include sales and purchases so there is an element of double counting, for example a dollar/yen trade would count twice.

However, the OECD said if Japan continues to reform its financial sector, scrapping barriers between banking and securities business and abandoning foreign exchange restrictions, a "tripolar system" with the dollar and euro could develop.

The OECD said while the yen is currently used significantly less internationally than its weight in world trade would suggest, increased trade with other Asian countries could give it a larger weight.
"The importance of the yen as a unit of account in trade, as a reserve currency and as a means of payment could eventually rise," the OECD said.
It said a similar argument applied to the euro and Central and Eastern Europe, given the close exchange rate links many countries in the region have adopted to the mark.

"Intensified private sector use could follow from closer links of these countries to the euro-area, which will most likely remain the predominant trading partner of central and Eastern European countries," it said.
"This would strengthen the euro's role as a currency of denomination and a means of payment but also feed back to the store of value function," the OECD said.
